NONE: C1 lack of ability to do something

example: [ + to infinitive ] Inability to use a computer is a serious disadvantage when you are applying for jobs.
不會使用電腦在求職時是個十分不利的條件。
Compare
disability

NONE: › very difficult or impossible to travel to

example: one of the most inaccessible places in the world
世界上最難到達的地方之一
Some of the houses on the hillside are inaccessible to cars.
山坡上的一些房屋開車上不去。
Why is opera so inaccessible to so many people?
為甚麼歌劇有這麼多人無法欣賞？
I found his lecture completely inaccessible.
我發覺他的講座完全聽不懂。

NONE: C1 a situation in which a fact or measurement is not completely correct or exact

example: The film is full of historical inaccuracies.
這部影片中許多地方與歷史不符。
The inaccuracy of the missiles greatly diminishes their effectiveness.
這些導彈的不精確性大大減弱了其效果。

NONE: B2 not completely correct or exact, or not able to do something correctly or exactly

example: Their estimate of the cost of the project was wildly (= extremely) inaccurate.
他們對專案費用的估計非常不準確。
an inaccurate device/weapon
不精確的設備／武器

NONE: › failure to do anything that might provide a solution to a problem

example: The West's inaction has put millions of people at risk of starvation.
西方世界不採取行動，導致數以百萬計的人面臨飢餓的威脅。
This announcement follows months of inaction and delay.
這個聲明是在數月的不作為和延遲後發表的。

NONE: 無行動的，不活動的，不活躍的

example: It's bad for your health to be physically inactive.
不活動筋骨對健康不好。
The property market remains largely inactive.
房地產市場仍很不活躍。

C or U: › [ C or U ] the fact that something is not good enough or is too small in amount
U: › [ U ] a lack of confidence that makes you feel unable to deal with a situation

example: Economic growth is hindered by the inadequacies of the public transport system.
經濟發展受制於公共交通運輸系統的不完善。
The inadequacy of the budget is likely to cause problems.
預算的不足有可能會導致問題。
I always suffer from feelings of inadequacy when I'm with him.
和他在一起時總覺得自己不如他，這讓我感到不舒服。

NONE: C1 not good enough or too low in quality
› not confident enough to deal with a situation

example: This work is woefully (= extremely) inadequate - you'll have to do it again.
這工作做得非常糟糕——你必須重做。
She rejected the $2 million offer as totally inadequate.
她認為200萬美元的出價完全不夠，因而拒絕了。
Maddie's a real expert on art, so I feel completely inadequate whenever I talk to her about it.
麥迪在藝術方面是個真正的專家，因此每次和她談論藝術我都覺得自己不夠格。

NONE: › unable to be accepted in a law court
（在法庭上）不可接受的，不能採信的

example: Her confession was ruled inadmissible as evidence because it was given under pressure from the police.
她的供詞是在警方施壓下作出的，因此被判定不能作為證據。
All authors need to be wary of inadvertent copying of other people's ideas.
所有作者都需注意不要在無意中抄襲了他人的觀點。

NONE: › unwise and likely to have unwanted results, and therefore worth avoiding

example: Skiing is inadvisable if you have a weak heart.
如果你心臟不好，那麼去滑雪可不是好事。
It is inadvisable to generalize from the results of a single experiment.
單憑一個實驗的結果就進行概括是不妥當的。

NONE: 不可剝奪的；不可分割的

example: an inalienable right
不可剝奪的權利

NONE: › a woman someone is in love with

example: He's had a tattoo with the name of a former lover removed, to avoid hurting the feelings of his current inamorata.
為了不想傷現在情人的心，他把刺有舊情人名字的紋身去掉了。

NONE: › extremely silly or with no real meaning or importance
極其愚蠢的；無意義的；無聊的

example: He's always making inane remarks.
他老是發表愚蠢空洞的言論。
There are too many inane quiz shows on television these days.
現在電視上無聊的智力遊戲節目太多。

NONE: › having none of the characteristics of life that an animal or plant has

example: He looks at me as if I'm an inanimate object.
他看著我的樣子好像我是個沒有生命的物體。

NONE: › not directed at, intended for, or suitable for someone or something

example: These regulations are inapplicable to visitors from outside the European Community.
這些規定不適用於來自歐盟以外的遊客。

NONE: › the fact that a word or phrase does not sound natural and is not acceptable when used in a particular situation

example: Native speakers have a general sense of the appropriacy and inappropriacy of language.
說母語的人對措詞恰當與否大致有感覺。
His casual behaviour was wholly inappropriate for such a formal occasion.
他隨便的舉止在這樣正式的場合十分不恰當。
I think it would be inappropriate (for you) to invite her to a party so soon after her husband's death.
我認為（你）在她丈夫剛去世不久就邀請她參加聚會是不合適的。
His comments were perhaps inapt.
他的評論可能不合時宜。

NONE: › unable to express feelings or ideas clearly, or expressed in a way that is difficult to understand
不善辭令的，口齒不清的

example: When it comes to expressing their emotions, some people are hopelessly inarticulate.
一些人在表達自己的感情時顯得笨嘴拙舌。
His speech was inarticulate and it was obvious he had been drinking.
他講話口齒不清，很明顯他喝酒了。

NONE: › used to introduce a phrase that explains why or how much something described in another part of the sentence is true

example: Inasmuch as you are their commanding officer, you are responsible for the behaviour of these men.
由於你是這些士兵的指揮官，你就要對他們的行為負責。
Her disappointing exam results are entirely due to her inattention in class.
她考試成績如此令人失望，完全是由於上課時不專心。

NONE: › not giving attention to someone or something

example: He was wholly inattentive to the needs of his children.
他對子女的需求全然不顧。
The noise of the machinery made her voice inaudible.
機器的噪音淹沒了她的聲音。

NONE: › An inaugural speech is the first speech someone gives when starting an important new job.
› An inaugural event is the first in a series of planned events.

example: the president's inaugural address to the nation
總統向全國發表的就職演說
the inaugural meeting of the archaeological society
考古組織的第一次會議

NONE: › to put someone into an official position with a ceremony
使正式就職，為…舉行就職典禮
› to put something into use or action officially
› to mark the beginning of a new period, style, or activity
開創（新時代）；開始（新風尚或新活動）

example: The change of government inaugurated a new era of economic prosperity.
政府的變革開創了經濟繁榮的新時代。

NONE: › in the US, the day when a person officially becomes president in a special ceremony and takes responsibility from the previous president
美國總統就職日（美國總統從前任總統接過權力，正式就職，舉行就職儀式的日子）
› showing signs that something will not be successful or positive

example: After an inauspicious start, Scotland went on to win the match.
蘇格蘭隊開場不順，但後來還是贏了比賽。
